name: 1721 Prairie Avenue — Wirt Dexter house, Arthur Little's front of 1889, K01 frontage assembly

grade.why: Pictured: 5 of the pictures on the Images tab show it.

documented_range.note: The 1891 plate shows Arthur Little's front of 1889; the 1911 sheet draws the same plan and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). The c. 1888 photographs show the house before that front and are not this phase.

placement.position_note: The rear north corner of the K01 main body: the draft's origin carried 3.8 m north to the main block's north wall (the trace at draft v -3.75 to -3.9), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet, whose own residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation 179.607 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's rear-to-street line; v runs SOUTH, from the north wall toward 1729.
placement.symbolic_location: 1721 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1721 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).

footprint.note: The main block read off the 1911 sheet's trace (s20fp-1721-b1 p1) in the house's frame: its rear wall at u 0, the recessed wall behind the porch at u 7.7-7.75, its north wall at v 0 (the trace at -0.05 to 0.1 once carried), its south wall at v 17.6 (the trace at 17.6-17.8). The forward block, its bows and the rear wing stand on it (form.bays, form.rear_wings).

stories.note: '3B' printed on the 1911 sheet; the 1891 plate shows three storeys over a low basement.

construction.note: The 1911 sheet colours the main block and its rear wing brick. The plate shows the wall light and smooth.

principal_floor_m.note: The plate's porch stands six or so risers over the walk and its basement lights are at the walk: about 1.3 m.

storey_heights_m.note: Read off the plate in proportion to the porch's columns and the ground-floor windows: a tall principal storey, a second a little lower, a third under the cornice lower again.

service_wall_brick.note: A buff brick: the plate shows the walls light, much lighter than the red and brown brick of the houses beside it. Its exact colour is not read.

wall_finish.note: The plate draws every face light and smooth, with no brick courses on a print sharp enough to show the shutters' slats and the neighbours' brick, so the brick is taken as painted (or laid in a pale brick the kit does not carry). The plate is monochrome: the pale buff is chosen, not read.

street_front_trim.note: The plate's windows have small carved tablets over their heads; a cornice hood stands for them until T-1879 carves them.

wall_head.note: The plate's deep moulded cornice. Its modillions and the balustraded parapet over it are T-1879's.

roof_form.note: The plate shows no roof over the parapet from the street: a flat deck behind it.

eave_overhang_m.note: The plate's cornice stands well out of the wall.

window_kit.note: The kit's sash; the plate's windows are many-paned sash, T-1879's to glaze.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: The porch's floor fills the recess to the front's line, as the 1911 sheet draws the porch (2.9 m by 3.5 m) and the plate shows it.

stoop_width_m.note: The plate's steps run the porch's width between its columns.

entrance_bay.note: The door is in the recessed north part of the front (K01's low-v end: v runs south here, from the north wall), under the porch, on the plate.

front_bays.note: The recessed wall's one bay: the door, and a window over it in each upper storey (the plate).

side_bays.note: The north wall of the main block: the plate shows a window a storey near its front; the rest is hidden by the house to the north.

north_bays.note: The south wall toward 1729: no picture shows it.

rear_bays.note: The rear wall beside the rear wing: no picture shows it.

sash_by_storey.note: The plate's tall ground-floor and second-storey windows and the shorter third.

basement_lights.note: The plate's low basement lights at the walk.

chimneys.note: The plate's tall plain stack rising past the parapet at the forward block's north return, stood on the main block's front wall behind it; the second stack is the rules' and no picture shows it.

entrance_kit.note: The plate's porch: two round columns at its front corners, a flat roof under a deep fascia and cornice, railed as a balcony at the second floor, filling the recess to the front block's line. The rail is balustered on the plate; the kit's railing stands for it.

windows.why_not_ordinary: the ground floor's tall lights: the plate shows tall shuttered windows over iron balconettes in a 5.6 m principal storey, taller than the rules' ordinary sash
the ground floor's tall lights: the plate shows tall shuttered windows over iron balconettes in a 5.6 m principal storey, taller than the rules' ordinary sash
the ground floor's tall lights: the plate shows tall shuttered windows over iron balconettes in a 5.6 m principal storey, taller than the rules' ordinary sash

bays.note: The 1911 sheet's front (trace s20fp-1721-b1 p1 in this frame): the forward block's face at u 10.6, 2.9 m before the recessed wall at u 7.7, from v 3.55 (its north return, beside the porch) to the south wall at v 17.6; the north bow from v 4.8 to 9.4, 1.2 m out, the south bow from v 12.6 to 17.0, 1.1 m out. The plate shows the block, both bows rising through the ground and second storeys and each roofed at the third floor (its balustrade is T-1879's); the windows' places on the bows and between them are read off the plate, their count to a face reconstructed. The bows' outer windows stand at 36 degrees (north) and 32 degrees (south) off the bow's centre, pulled in from 40 so that each recess stays inside its bow (the K08 kit's recess rule); the plate places them near each bow's ends without fixing an angle.

rear_wings.note: The 1911 sheet's 'long 2B brick rear wing with 1-storey frame pieces at both ends' (census s20-1721-a1): the brick wing from the main rear wall to u -19.9, from the north wall (v 0) to v 6.2; the frame pieces at its east end (trace p3, p4) as one frame room to u -22.4. Its windows are reconstructed: no picture shows it.

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B brick dwelling (D) with two curved bays on the Prairie face'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1840 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

built.note: The marker: 'Wirt Dexter Residence. Built 1863'. The house was remodelled later.

citations.citation: 'Lost Houses of Prairie Avenue: 1600-1700 Blocks', Prairie Avenue Historic District interpretive marker, Chicago; transcription on the Historical Marker Database (HMdb), marker 308722.
what_it_supplies: each house's builder, year built and architect as the district's marker gives them
Pullman's theatre, organ and bowling alley and Beman's conservatory additions, in paraphrase

what_it_supplies: the recess at the north end of the front, the entrance porch standing in it on two columns and its flat roof railed as a balcony
the forward block with two bows through two storeys, each topped by a balcony at the third floor
three storeys over a low basement, a flat roof behind a moulded cornice and a balustraded parapet
the tall stack on the forward block's north return
what_it_does_not_supply: the plan's sizes: the 1911 Sanborn sheet's trace controls them
the south side, the rear and the long rear wing

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 20.
what_it_supplies: The Illinois Central / Michigan Central right-of-way and, from the 16th Street row south about 60 m, the water's edge beside it, as of 1911
Footprints, lot lines, street widths (66 ft; 16th Street 50 ft), addresses, material by colour and story counts for Indiana Av. to the tracks, 16th to 18th Street, as of 1911
Its own printed Scale of Feet, which the georeference uses as its scale
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: T-1878 (package N18A of T-1837) refines the district draft (T-2335) in place under this id onto the K01 kit: the 1911 sheet's plan (the main block with its north part recessed behind an entrance porch, the forward block with two bows, the long 2B rear wing and its frame end) read against the 1891 Inland Architect plate of Arthur Little's front. Its carving, the balustraded parapet and the bows' balconies, shutters, balconettes and the image gate are T-1879's. docs/RESEARCH/k01-1721-dexter-1878/README.md is the reading.
